allow_large: Two code files plus tests, a decision record and synced skill copies; under the rule already on main (tests and sync output don't count) it is within the limit, but the installed release still counts them
done_when: Before each Codex thread start or resume, Forge asks the app-server for the checkout's project hooks; each hook whose definition is exactly what forge sync writes for this repo is passed to the turn as trusted (its current hash in the thread config's hooks state), so the guard and the other Forge hooks run on every worker and reader turn; if any project hook is not trusted and differs from Forge's own, the turn stops with one plain line naming the hook and how to review it in Codex's /hooks, changing nothing. Decision 0102 records the owner's choice and supersedes decision 0082 for Forge's own hooks. Command-level tests with the stub app-server: Forge's own untrusted hooks are trusted and the turn starts with them; a modified or foreign untrusted hook stops the turn.

findings.body: When Codex's config trusts the main repository but explicitly marks a linked worktree untrusted, this prerequisite still succeeds: `src/forge/doctor.py:75–82` accepts either path being trusted. New external evidence in [Codex 0.159.2's trust resolver](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/refs/tags/rust-v0.159.2/codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs) (`decision_for_dir`, lines 985–1016) shows that the checkout's explicit entry takes precedence over main-repository trust. Codex therefore excludes project hooks while Forge proceeds to start the turn with an empty hook listing. This affects the newly gated `forge read` and `forge ask` paths, as well as the shared worker path. The stub repeats the same permissive check at `tests/stubs/codex-app-server:97–100`, so the current tests hide the discrepancy. Honor an explicit checkout trust decision before falling back to main-repository trust, and cover conflicting entries through a Forge command.
findings.title: Respect explicit worktree distrust before inheriting repository trust

why: Forge's Codex workers run with no Forge hooks at all, the destructive-command guard included: Codex silently skips project hooks that aren't trusted, and every change to a hook un-trusts it, so the guard has not protected Codex worker turns since the hook launcher changed
